text: This capstone doesn't introduce anything new. It's the same handful of ideas from this whole course — features, a train/test split, a model that fits the data, honest evaluation — run start to finish, by you, on one real dataset, over the next three lessons.

Five steps. Load and split the data. Scale it and train a baseline model. Predict on data the model has never seen. Evaluate honestly — every metric, not just the flattering one. Present it the way you'd show it in a portfolio. Each step maps straight back to a chapter you already finished.
Everything here is pandas and scikit-learn — if you worked through lessons 22 through 26, both are already installed. The dataset is built into scikit-learn itself, so there's nothing to download.

The dataset is Breast Cancer Wisconsin, Diagnostic: five hundred sixty-nine real tumor samples, thirty numeric measurements each, labeled malignant or benign by actual pathologists. Three hundred fifty-seven benign, two hundred twelve malignant. Small, clean, and a real binary classification task — the lesson time goes to the ML decisions, not data cleanup.

Three ground rules before any code runs. No peeking — the scaler gets fit on the training data only. No cherry-picking — every metric gets reported, not just the best one. And one honest baseline — a simple, interpretable model, chosen on purpose, the same way this course introduced classification back in chapter two.
Lesson 28 is where the real code starts: splitting this data correctly, and training the first model on it.
